TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantees for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Establish non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for KernelSHAP, proving upper bounds on the number of subset evaluations required to achieve a given accuracy in estimating Shapley values. This involves formulating a new sub-Gaussian regression estimator for the constrained weighted least-squares problem at the heart of KernelSHAP, and then analyzing its properties to derive finite-sample bounds. As a byproduct, we also provide sample-complexity guarantees for the family of randomized estimators related to KernelSHAP, including those that sample subsets with or without replacement.
CONTROLS: Baseline: asymptotic analysis of existing estimators, Abelian: vanilla KernelSHAP (no subsampling or resampling), Ablation: subsampling alone, Resampling alone
COST: 5400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Strong convergence rate is expected for linear models and poor performance for highly complex models, where the number of features greatly exceeds sample size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Analyzing KernelSHAP and Related Estimators
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework for analyzing KernelSHAP and related estimators, which enables a systematic comparison of their performance in terms of sample complexity and computational efficiency. This framework is based on a stochastic optimization perspective, viewing the estimators as solvers to a constrained convex optimization problem with a curved feasible set. By leveraging tools from stochastic optimization, we derive a series of metrics to quantify the curvature of the constrained convex program, which directly relate to the sample complexity and computational efficiency of the estimators.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing analysis of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, Abelian: InterpolatedSHAP (subsets sampled with or without replacement), Ablation: regression formulation alone, Weight analysis alone
COST: 12600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The unified framework will reveal that the choice of sampling distribution affects not only the bias but also the variance of the estimator, and that high curvature of the feasible set leads to high sample complexity. KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP may perform similarly under low curvature conditions but will differ in high-dimensional or noisy scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LeverageSHAP: A Lower-Bound Approach to Analyzing its Sample Complexity
PROPOSAL: Investigate the sample complexity of LeverageSHAP by modeling its behavior as a lower-bound approach, sampling subsets based on their statistical leverage scores. This involves reformulating the constrained weighted least-squares problem as a linear regression problem and applying tools from randomized linear algebra to bound the estimation error and sample complexity. Through this framework, we derive non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for LeverageSHAP and assess its trade-offs against KernelSHAP in both theory and experiments.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing analysis of LeverageSHAP, Abelian: InterpolatedSHAP (subsets sampled with or without replacement), Ablation: regression formulation alone, Sampling alone
COST: 8820 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: LeverageSHAP will outperform KernelSHAP in specific settings with well-conditioned problem instances, but its overall performance may degrade in scenarios with a large number of redundant features. LeverageSHAP is likely to exhibit a lower convergence rate compared to KernelSHAP due to the constraints imposed by leveraging the scores for row sampling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exact and Efficient Computation of Shapley Values for Linear Regression
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of exactly and efficiently computing Shapley values for linear regression, using the linear model as a subroutine to compute the Shapley values in a highly efficient manner. This involves expressing the model's output as a linear combination of the input features, allowing for the direct computation of the Shapley values. A further practical improvement will be to generalize this approach to other types of structured models, effectively outsourcing the Shapley value computation to an existing solver or model.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing approach to Shapley value computation, Abelian: linear regression reformulation, Ablation: specific structured models alone, Regression-specific enhancements alone
COST: 4050 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Efficient computation will be observed for linear models with a low feature dimension, and will possibly be generalized to other types of low-dimensional linear models. Linear regression-based computation of Shapley values may lead to a potential performance drop in comparison to more complex models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distributed and Parallel Computation of Shapley Values for Large-Scale Datasets
PROPOSAL: Investigate the challenges and opportunities associated with distributed and parallel computation of Shapley values, particularly in scenarios involving massive datasets. This involves designing and evaluating a parallel computing framework that efficiently distributes the computation across a cluster or a cloud environment, leveraging existing parallelization libraries such as PyTorch-Distributed and Horovod. We also investigate strategies to optimize the computation, such as data pruning and partial computations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing frameworks for model computation, Abelian: distributed randomized estimators, Ablation: parallelization library alone, Data pruning alone
COST: 10800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed framework to achieve a significant speedup for large-scale datasets and show that parallelization techniques can mitigate the computational bottlenecks associated with Shapley value computation. However, potential errors may arise from synchronized sampling methods or data anomalies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extending KernelSHAP to Handle Discrete and Mixed-Type Features
PROPOSAL: Generalize KernelSHAP to accommodate discrete and mixed-type features, which often occur in real-world datasets, by incorporating kernel functions specifically designed for these types of features. This will enable the application of Shapley values to a broader range of problems and datasets, extending the explanatory power of this method. The proposed extension will leverage insights from kernel methods, feature learning, and feature transformations to develop an efficient and scalable algorithm.
CONTROLS: Baseline: original KernelSHAP, Abelian: kernel functions for discrete and mixed-type features, Ablation: continuous kernel functions alone, Transformation methods alone
COST: 16200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the extended version of KernelSHAP will provide more accurate explanations for models with complex feature types and highlight the importance of handling non-nominal features in feature importance analysis. However, its performance may degrade for problems with extremely high-dimensional or highly correlated features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Empirical Study on the Sensitivity of Shapley Value Estimators to Hyperparameters
PROPOSAL: Conduct an in-depth, comprehensive study to analyze the sensitivity of KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and other existing Shapley value estimators to their hyperparameters, such as the kernel type, the number of samples, and the regularization strength. This involves systematically varying these hyperparameters to investigate their impact on the accuracy and computational efficiency of the estimators, as well as their effect on the interpretability of the resulting explanations. Such an analysis will help identify robust and efficient configurations of the estimators and provide insights into the design of automated hyperparameter tuning methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing implementations of Shapley value estimators, Abelian: Grid search hyperparameter tuning, Ablation: individual hyperparameter analysis alone, Automatic hyperparameter tuning alone
COST: 9450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our results indicate that most Shapley value estimators are highly sensitive to their hyperparameters, and unexpected suboptimal configurations can lead to poor performance. Tuning hyperparameters will be crucial for achieving reliable and efficient explanations, highlighting the importance of correctly setting these parameters to prevent suboptimal models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularization Techniques for Improving the Stability of Shapley Value Estimators
PROPOSAL: Investigate regularization techniques for improving the stability and robustness of Shapley value estimators, which are crucial for reliable and interpretable model explanations. This involves adapting and extending existing regularization methods from the machine learning and optimization communities to the constrained weighted least-squares problem in Shapley value estimation. We examine the impact of various regularization strategies on the accuracy, stability, and computational efficiency of the estimators, and develop new techniques tailored to the specific needs of Shapley value estimation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: original Shapley value estimators, Abelian: L1 and L2 regularization, Ablation: Elastic Net regularization alone, Group Lasso alone
COST: 13500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Regularization techniques will significantly improve the stability of Shapley value estimators and enable them to provide more robust and reliable explanations, particularly in noisy and high-dimensional settings. The most effective techniques will be likely to be those that combine different forms of regularization to adapt to diverse data and model characteristics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Examples for Shapley Value Estimators: Attacking and Defending Model Explanations
PROPOSAL: Introduce the concept of adversarial examples for Shapley value estimators, where the goal is to find input samples that, when provided to the explainer, produce misleading or toy explanations. We develop novel methods for crafting these examples and propose strategies for defending against them, such as using robust estimators, outlier detection, or incorporating ensembling methods. This investigation highlights the importance of considering the security and trustworthiness of Shapley value explanations in practice.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing Shapley value estimators, Abelian: projected gradient descent attack, Ablation: fast gradient sign method alone, Statistical analysis for defense alone
COST: 18000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The existence of adversarial examples will have a significant impact on the adoption and trustworthiness of Shapley value explanations, and our proposed defenses will provide essential tools for protecting against such attacks, enabling more reliable and useful explanations.

TITLE: A Software Framework for Scalable and Robust Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive software framework that integrates and extends the proposed solutions, enabling efficient, scalable, and robust Shapley value estimation for a wide range of applications. This framework will incorporate modular and extensible design principles, as well as flexible configuration options, to accommodate different problem settings and model types. We aim to make the framework publicly available and widely usable.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing frameworks, Abelian: unified implementation, Ablation: separate components alone
COST: 32400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our framework will significantly accelerate the widespread adoption of Shapley value explanations and provide researchers and practitioners with a robust and scalable tool for interpreting complex models, ultimately enhancing the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning models.

TITLE: Modulating a Video-Capable Multimodal Large Language Model for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify a pre-trained video-capable MLLM (e.g.,the video-conditional version of BetterMM,  an extension of the Better ОднаValleyWays-00large-scale MLLM) to incorporate temporal change comprehension. We will add a custom sequence-to-sequence module to the MLLM's decoder, which incorporates features extracted from a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for image and video classification. This module will condition the language generation on the temporal evolution of the scene. The final generated description will be polished by another MLLM decoding step, ensuring consistency and fluency.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be a standard pre-trained video-capable MLLM, without the custom sequence-to-sequence module. We also plan to ablate the CNN features and evaluate the quality of the descriptions without them.
COST: 15000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This modulated MLLM will significantly outperform the baseline on both tasks, demonstrating improved understanding of temporal change dynamics and more accurate descriptions. However, its performance might degrade when generating descriptions for long มห sequences, due to the challenges of long-range temporal reasoning.

TITLE: Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting using Diffusion-based Generators with Conditional Language Guidance
PROPOSAL: Train a diffusion-based image generator (e.g., the popular DALL-E model) to forecast future satellite images, conditioned on historical sequences and natural-language descriptions of the changes observed in those sequences. The language guidance will be provided by a separate MLLM and will be used to fine-tune the diffusion generator's outputs to ensure temporal consistency.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our diffusion-based generator to a standard diffusion model, without conditional language guidance. Additionally, we will ablate the MLLM's role in the generation process to assess its contribution to temporal consistency.
COST: 18000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will yield state-of-the-art results in future satellite image forecasting, with significant improvements in temporal consistency. However, the model's performance might suffer from mode collapse, where the generator produces limited variations of the same forecast, due to the challenges of training diffusion models on large-scale datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Long-Range Temporal Dependency-Aware CNN for Extracting Change-Causal Features from Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Design a custom CNN that learns to extract features from satellite image time series, focusing on capturing long-range temporal dependencies and change-causal relationships between images. The architecture will incorporate temporal convolutional layers, graph convolutional layers, and a self-attention mechanism to enable the model to understand the temporal evolution of scenes and identify underlying causal factors of change.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our custom CNN to a standard CNN (e.g., ResNet50) and an existing state-of-the-art graph convolutional network for this task. Additionally, we will assess the impact of each component of the custom CNN on its performance using ablation studies.
COST: 22000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed CNN will significantly improve the extraction of change-causal features from satellite image time series, enabling better understanding of temporal change dynamics and more accurate language descriptions. However, training and testing the model might be computationally expensive due to the large size of the feature extractor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasting using Segmentation-Based Metrics
PROPOSAL: Develop a suite of segmentation-based metrics to evaluate the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts. These metrics will assess how well the generated forecast integrates with the historical sequence, focusing on measures such as completeness, continuity, and coherence of changes. We will compare the performance of our proposed metrics to existing image-quality metrics (e.g., PSNR, SSIM) using a variety of evaluation setups.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be a standard set of image-quality metrics. We will also assess the impact of our segmentation-based metrics on the ranking of forecast models using a correlation study.
COST: 10000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed segmentation-based metrics will provide more nuanced evaluations of temporal consistency in satellite image forecasting, better capturing the essence of what makes a forecast temporally consistent. However, the metrics might be sensitive to the specific changes observed in the historical sequence, requiring careful calibration and tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting: Cross-Domain Adaptation for Land-Use Change Monitoring
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of transfer learning for satellite image time series forecasting, leveraging pre-trained models and adaptation techniques to facilitate cross-domain adaptation. We will explore ways to adapt a pre-trained model, trained on a different satellite image dataset, to a new target domain (e.g., land-use change monitoring) with minimal additional training data.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be a model trained from scratch on the target domain. We will also compare the performance of different adaptation techniques, such as domain-invariant feature learning and multi-task learning.
COST: 25000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will enable more efficient forecasting of satellite image time series in new domains, leveraging prior knowledge from other datasets and reducing the need for extensive retraining. However, the success of transfer learning will heavily depend on the degree of domain similarity between the source and target datasets.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE:  Cross-Domain Adaptation for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting: A Study on Land-Use Change Monitoring
PROPOSAL: Modify the transfer learning proposal to focus on a specific land-use change monitoring task, where the goal is to predict land-cover changes from satellite image time series. We will collect a new dataset of land-cover changes from satellite images and use it to adapt a pre-trained model, exploring different adaptation techniques such as domain-invariant feature learning and multi-task learning. The adapted model will then be evaluated on a separate test set of land-cover changes.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be a model trained from scratch on the land-cover change dataset. We will also compare the performance of different pre-trained models and adaptation techniques.
COST: 18000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised approach will demonstrate the effectiveness of transfer learning in land-use change monitoring, leveraging prior knowledge from other satellite image datasets and adapting it to the specific task of land-cover change prediction. However, the results might be sensitive to the quality of the adaptation process and the pre-trained model used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding Change Agency in Satellite Image Time Series using Temporal Graph Attention Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a Temporal Graph Attention Network (TGAN) to model the temporal evolution of a scene in satellite image time series and identify changes caused by specific agents (e.g., construction, agriculture, or climate events). The TGAN will learn to weight the importance of different nodes in the graph (representing images, agents, or other relevant information) and edges (representing temporal relationships) to predict change agency.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our TGAN to a standard graph convolutional network (GCN) and a recurrent neural network (RNN) using graph-structured input data. Additionally, we will evaluate the quality of change agency predictions using metrics such as precision, recall, and F1-score.
COST: 28000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will enable better understanding of change agency in satellite image time series, improving the accuracy of change predictions and providing valuable information for decision-making. However, the performance of the TGAN might be affected by the quality of the graph-structured input data and the choice of model hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Fusion for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting in Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Develop a multimodal fusion framework to integrate multiple sources of information (e.g., satellite images, climate data, and socioeconomic indicators) for temporal change description and forecasting in satellite image time series. The framework will use a combination of attention mechanisms and graph neural networks to learn the relationships between different modalities and predict the future evolution of a scene.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our multimodal fusion framework to a single-modal approach (using only satellite images) and a baseline model that does not incorporate multimodal fusion. Additionally, we will assess the impact of different modalities on the performance of the framework using ablation studies.
COST: 32000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve the accuracy of temporal change description and forecasting in satellite image time series by incorporating multiple sources of information and learning their relationships. However, the performance of the framework might be sensitive to the quality and availability of the multimodal data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Temporal Change Description and Forecasting using Uncertainty-aware Multimodal Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop an uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion framework to predict the uncertainty of temporal change descriptions and forecasts in satellite image time series. The framework will use a combination of Monte Carlo dropout and Bayesian neural networks to learn the uncertainty of the predictions and provide more robust and reliable results.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion framework to a standard multimodal fusion approach and a baseline model that does not incorporate uncertainty-awareness. Additionally, we will evaluate the quality of the uncertainty predictions using metrics such as expected calibration error and interval coverage probability.
COST: 36000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve the robustness and reliability of temporal change description and forecasting in satellite image time series by incorporating uncertainty-awareness and predicting the uncertainty of the predictions. However, the performance of the framework might be affected by the choice of uncertainty-awareness techniques and the availability of sufficient training data.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE:  Modulating a Video-Capable Multimodal Large Language Model with Uncertainty-awareness for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify the video-capable multimodal large language model to incorporate uncertainty-awareness, enabling it to predict the uncertainty of temporal change descriptions and forecasts in satellite image time series. The model will use a combination of Monte Carlo dropout and Bayesian neural networks to learn the uncertainty of the predictions and provide more robust and reliable results.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the revised model to the original model and a baseline model that does not incorporate uncertainty-awareness. Additionally, we will evaluate the quality of the uncertainty predictions using metrics such as expected calibration error and interval coverage probability.
COST: 24000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised model will improve the robustness and reliability of temporal change description and forecasting in satellite image time series, leveraging the strength of the original model and incorporating uncertainty-awareness to provide more accurate and reliable results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Updating Different Model Components on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment where we update different components of a pre-trained forecasting model online, such as the final prediction layer, adapters attached to the model's input or output, and the entire model's weights, on a variety of tasks including traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting. We will compare the performance of these different updating schemes using a range of evaluation metrics, including mean absolute error and mean squared error.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the updating schemes against a baseline where the entire model's weights are frozen and no updates are made.
COST: 5000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that updating the final prediction layer will perform well, but may not be sufficient to capture complex distribution shifts, while updating the entire model's weights may be too unstable and lead to poor performance.

TITLE: Evaluating the Performance of Online Gradient Descent with Batch Averaging on Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the performance of online gradient descent with batch averaging on multi-step forecasting, where the model forecasts H steps ahead and the true values for the forecast are not available until time t+H. We will test this approach using a pre-trained model on traffic flow forecasting and solar power forecasting datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of online gradient descent with batch averaging against the baseline of freezing the model's weights and no updates, as well as our previous experiment (proposal 1).
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that online gradient descent with batch averaging will outperform the baseline and provide more stable updates, but the performance may degrade as H increases due to the delayed feedback.

TITLE: Comparing the Robustness of Online Time Series Forecasting Methods to Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of different online time series forecasting methods to concept drift using synthetic data with abrupt and gradual changes in the underlying patterns. We will compare the performance of state-of-the-art methods such as OGD, OGD with batch averaging, and model-based advice with our novel approach that combines these methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the methods against the baseline of freezing the model's weights and no updates, as well as our previous experiments (proposals 1 and 2).
COST: 7000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that our novel approach will outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of robustness to concept drift, but the performance may degrade in certain scenarios with high variance in the data.

TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Late-Interaction vs Embed-and-Lift Multimodal Retrieval in Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We'll conduct an experiment comparing the performance of ColPali-based late-interaction multimodal retrievers with embed-and-lift implementations on the dual-purpose passage-ranking and document-ranking protocol of the MS MARCO v1 dataset with the DELIGHTv2 evaluation, focusing on the settings that typically matter most for practical retrieval: average Precision@10, recall and latency at various ranks. We'll also evaluate online latency and storage requirements for the two models using real-world data and indices.
CONTROLS: We'll compare against the current state-of-the-art ColPali-based retriever, as well as an unaltered existing embed-and-lift retriever baseline.
